newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uighurs protest in Kazakhstan against China.
newsitem.headline: Uighurs protest in Kazakhstan against China.

text.p: Ethnic Uighurs staged a noisy protest outside the Chinese embassy in Kazakhstan on Thursday against what they said was Beijing's intention to execute Uighur students arrested over last month's riots in Xinjiang province.

The group of about 35 young Uighurs shouted "East Turkestan!", the Moslem Uighurs' name for China's troubled northwest province, and "Allah akbar!", or "God is great". Chinese diplomats filmed the protesters with video recorders.

Officials in Xinjiang said on Thursday they had indicted six people in connection with the anti-Chinese rioting in the province but denied allegations made by exiled Uighur separatists that China would execute two rioters.

The United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan said on Wednesday it had received information about the executions from its "secret sources". Information from the remote Chinese region is difficult to verify.
The group named the two Uighurs as Abu Khair and Abdu Medchit, both around 25 years old. They would probably face a firing squad in Urumqi, regional capital of Xinjiang, it said.
The Front is one of several Uighur organisations fighting for an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, home to a majority of Turkic-speaking Moslems like the ethnic Uighurs.
